rationale: The runtime is not a stable replaceable interpreter boundary. It combines scheduling, mutable executor registration, input expression evaluation, hidden provider/search effects, status/event/result mutation, and AgentSession projection. Provider errors and even permission denial can become degraded node results that the runtime marks succeeded, while raised failures follow a different path. It lacks durable claims, exact effect receipts, retry/reconciliation, typed failure variants, and uniform authority enforcement. Preserve behavior fixtures and observable payload examples, but reimplement the capability over typed Programs, explicit ports, durable run/step semantics, and reducer-based recovery.

rationale: The store cannot be adapted as a canonical durable replay boundary. It maintains mutable snapshot status/results and append-only events as separate truths, commits each mutation independently, cannot event-rebuild results, and makes stateful replay a snapshot echo. SQL create_run resets an existing run snapshot without clearing its previous events, unlike the in-memory implementation. Event sequence allocation uses max(seq)+1 without locking/retry, public rows are not project-scoped, constructors perform DDL, and configured fallback can replace durability with fresh process memory. Preserve fixtures and legacy observation shapes only; implement a project-scoped journal and pure reducer with exact crash/replay semantics.

source_evidence.claim: C1.3 is locator-only, pending, non-authorizing, and C1 is not the fixed first migration.
The memory backend stores run snapshots, events, and results in three mutable dictionaries and returns their product as a snapshot.
SQL status, node status, results, and events are committed in separate sessions; event sequencing uses max(seq)+1.
Reusing an existing run_id resets status, node_statuses, metadata, and results but does not delete or bind off prior events, unlike InMemoryRunStore.create_run.
Public-schema snapshot and event tables have separate persisted truths, no project_key, and a unique run_id/seq event constraint.
The compiled store performs CREATE TABLE in its constructor and upserts globally keyed graph_id JSONB records.
Configuration may fail closed on SQL unavailability or replace the durable backend with a new in-memory store.
events_only replay derives only statuses; stateful mode returns stored events/results; consistency checking reports mismatches without rebuilding results or repairing state.
Store and replay tests use in-memory stores and prove snapshot retention/reload and mismatch detection, not SQL parity or exact recovery.
API replay tests mock the service result and validate envelope forwarding only; they do not exercise repository replay.
The architecture requires canonical-owner, resource, replay, memory/SQL observation, rollback, and reasoned P1 evidence before any P2 selection.
